site_name: TierPoint TekPark (former DBSi TEKPark Advanced Technology Center), 9999 Hamilton Blvd, Breinigsville, PA 18031
year_evidence_quote: Data Based Systems International, Inc. (DBSi) opened its third data center outside of Breinigsville, PA
year_site_match: The release names the facility as DBSi's "Hosting and Recovery Advanced Technology Center at TEKPark" outside Breinigsville, PA. Data Center Frontier (Breinigsville dateline, 2016-01-21) says the TierPoint TekPark building, a former Agere fab, "in 2011 was leased by DBSi (Data Based Systems International), which retrofitted the facility", then DBSi went to Xand (July 2012) and Xand to TierPoint (December 2014). TierPoint's TekPark campus page gives the address 9999 Hamilton Blvd, Breinigsville, PA 18031.
verification: Supports 2011 as claimed. The cited page is a third-party blog repost (posted 2013-04-16) of a DBSi PRWeb release datelined Bethlehem, PA, June 10, 2011; the release says the opening was marked by an open house "last week". I did not open the original PRWeb release, so the 2011 date rests on the dateline as reproduced in the repost, corroborated by the Data Center Frontier statement that DBSi leased and retrofitted the building in 2011. The release also says the facility was being commissioned in four phases with about half of phase one under contract, so 2011 dates the first phase only. The blog page gives no street address; the address tie comes from TierPoint's page plus the Data Center Frontier history. This dates the original converted building, not any later building on the campus.

site_name: CyrusOne San Antonio I (SAT1), 9999 Westover Hills Blvd, San Antonio, TX 78251
year_evidence_quote: its newest, 80,000-square-foot facility has been officially commissioned in San Antonio, Texas, and is open for business.
year_site_match: The release (dateline San Antonio, September 1, 2012) describes the facility as "the first enterprise-class multi-tenant data center in San Antonio". CyrusOne's own SAT1 page says "CyrusOne's 110,000-sq. ft. SAT1 data center was the city's first enterprise colocation facility" and places it "west of downtown San Antonio off state highway 151". The tie is by named facility (SAT1) through the operator's "first in the city" description, not by street address.
verification: Supports 2012 as claimed. REBusinessOnline (October 4, 2012) independently reports "CyrusOne has opened an 80,000-square-foot data center, located in San Antonio." Caveat on the address: no page I opened prints 9999 Westover Hills Blvd or the words Westover Hills; the match to SAT1 is an inference from CyrusOne's statement that SAT1 was the city's first enterprise colocation facility, combined with the 2012 release calling the new facility the first of its kind in San Antonio. The square footage differs between the 2012 release (80,000) and today's SAT1 page (110,000); I am uncertain why, and a later expansion is my inference, not something a page states. CyrusOne's SAT2-SAT4 campus page carries no opening dates, so I could not confirm on-page that those buildings came later. Three guessed URLs (a CyrusOne SAT2 page, a CyrusOne press-release page, a CyrusOne San Antonio market page) returned 404, a Data Center Knowledge URL returned an index page with no article, and a DatacenterDynamics URL returned 403; none were used.

lead.year_evidence_quote: its newest, 80,000-square-foot facility has been officially commissioned in San Antonio, Texas
lead.notes: A CyrusOne press release dated September 1, 2012 says its San Antonio facility has been officially commissioned. REBusinessOnline (October 4, 2012) reports CyrusOne 'has opened' an 80,000 sq ft San Antonio data center. The tie to SAT1: in 2012 this was CyrusOne's only San Antonio facility (SAT2 broke ground in 2014), and both CyrusOne's SAT1 page and the 2012 release call it the market's first enterprise facility. Neither page gives a street address. The TDLR record I opened (start 2/2014, completed 7/31/2016, closed) is SAT2 and was not used.
